notes.title: Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
text: Note 2 – Summary of significant accounting policies
Going concern

In assessing the Company’s liquidity and the substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern, the Company monitors and analyzes cash on hand and operating expenditure commitments. The Company’s liquidity needs are to meet working capital requirements and operating expense obligations. To date, the Company has financed its operations primarily through cash flows from contributions from stockholders, issuance of convertible notes from third parties and related parties, related party loans, and various public offerings.

The Company’s management has considered whether there is substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern due to: (1) recurring loss from operations of approximately $16.4 million for the year ended June 30, 2026; (2) accumulated deficit of approximately $72.5 million as of June 30, 2026; and (3) net operating cash outflow of approximately $6.9 million for the year ended June 30,2026. These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.

During the year ended June 30, 2026, the Company raised additional capital through various equity financing arrangements, including at-the-market offerings, share purchase arrangements, subscription agreements and a registered direct offering. Subsequent to June 30, 2026 and through the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Company continued to raise additional capital through equity financings, including net proceeds of approximately $1.0 million from its at-the-market offering and additional proceeds of $0.6 million pursuant to a subscription agreement.

Management plans to continue to seek additional equity financing and implement measures to manage operating expenditures to support the Company’s working capital requirements and meet its obligations as they become due. However, the Company’s ability to obtain additional financing is subject to uncertainty, and there can be no assurance that additional financing will be available on acceptable terms, or at all.

Despite receiving the net proceeds from the various offerings, the Company’s management is of the opinion that it will not have sufficient funds to meet the Company’s working capital requirements and debt obligations as they become due starting from one year from the date of this report due to the recurring loss. Therefore, management has determined that there is a substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. If the Company is unable to generate significant revenue, it may be required to curtail or cease its operations. Management is trying to alleviate the going concern risk through equity financing to support its working capital

notes.title: Business Combination
text: Note 3 – Business combination

On February 23, 2026, the Company entered into a Share Sale Agreement (the “SPA”) with Mohd Fadli Bin Wahab (the “Vendor”) to acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding share capital of TAZTE Technology Sdn. Bhd. (“TAZTE”) for cash consideration of RM1,000. TAZTE is a private company incorporated in Malaysia on March 8, 2024, and its principal activities include internet-based retail sales of products and the delivery of diverse food services.

On March 2, 2026, TADAA and the Vendor entered into a supplemental agreement that amended certain terms of the SPA, including requiring the Vendor to remain in office and maintain his position with TAZTE for a two-month transitional period commencing on February 23, 2026. The transitional period was completed on April 23, 2026. Upon satisfaction of the applicable closing requirements, the acquisition was completed on April 23, 2026, at which time the Company obtained control of TAZTE and TAZTE became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company. Accordingly, April 23, 2026 was determined to be the acquisition date for accounting purposes.

The Company’s acquisition of TAZTE was accounted for as a business combination in accordance with ASC 805, Business Combinations . The Company allocated the purchase price of TAZTE based upon the fair value of the identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed on the acquisition date. The Company estimated the fair values of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at the acquisition date in accordance with the business combination standard issued by the FASB using the fair value approach. Management of the Company is responsible for determining the fair value of assets acquired and liabilities assumed as of the acquisition date. Acquisition-related costs incurred for the acquisition were not material and were expensed as incurred in general and administrative expenses. The results of operations of TAZTE have been included in the Company’s consolidated financial statements beginning on April 23, 2026.

Based on assessments using the income test, asset test, and investment test pursuant to S-X Rule 3-05, the Company concluded that the acquisition of TAZTE was not significant. The acquisition did not exceed the applicable significance threshold under any of the three significance tests. Pursuant to ASC 805-10-50-2(h), the unaudited pro forma information of the Company for the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 set forth below gives effect to the business combination as if it had occurred on July 1, 2024 and combines the results of operations of the Company and TAZTE since then. The unaudited pro forma information is presented after applying the Company’s accounting policies and eliminating intra-entity transactions, as applicable. The unaudited pro forma information does not include any impact of transaction synergies and is presented for informational purposes only and is not necessarily indicative of the results of operations that would have occurred had the business combination been consummated as of that date or that may result in the future.

notes.title: Derivative Assets
text: Note 5 – Derivative assets
Contractual Right to Receive Shares – V Gallant

On October 29, 2024, the Company entered into a service agreement with V Gallant Sdn. Bhd. (“V Gallant”) to provide generative AI solutions and AI digital human technology services, which was subsequently amended to include AI cloud infrastructure services. On January 6, 2026, the Company and V Gallant mutually agreed to terminate the service agreement and related supplemental agreements. In connection with the termination, V Gallant agreed to compensate the Company in the amount of $5,200,000 through the issuance of 1,300,000 ordinary shares of V Gallant Limited at an agreed value of $4.00 per share. The shares were placed in escrow and remained subject to certain contractual conditions prior to their release to the Company.

The Company determined that it did not obtain control of the underlying shares and instead obtained a contractual right to receive the shares, which is accounted for as a derivative asset under ASC 815, Derivatives and Hedging . The fair value was determined with reference to an independent third-party valuation using primarily the discounted cash flow (“DCF”) method. The DCF valuation was based on projected cash flows for the financial years 2026 through 2030 and utilized a weighted average cost of capital (“WACC”) of 16.0% as a significant unobservable input, with terminal value determined using a perpetual-growth methodology. The contractual right was initially recognized at a fair value of $3,000,000. As of June 30, 2026, the DCF method indicated a value of $1.71 per underlying share, resulting in a fair value of the derivative asset of $2,223,000. The Company recognized a loss from the change in fair value of $777,000 for the year ended June 30, 2026. The derivative asset was classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.
Contractual Right to Receive Shares – Reveillon Group Limited (“RG”)

On December 22, 2025, the Company entered into a Share Sale Agreement with a third party to dispose of its entire equity interest in TADAA Ventures and its subsidiary, Bowlcrafted, in exchange for 700,000 ordinary shares of Reveillon Group Limited (“RG Shares”) with an agreed aggregate value of $1,400,000. The RG Shares were placed in escrow and remained subject to certain contractual conditions and restrictions prior to their release to the Company.

The Company determined that it did not obtain control of the underlying RG Shares and instead obtained a contractual right associated with the shares, which is accounted for as a derivative asset under ASC 815. The fair value was determined with reference to an independent third-party valuation using primarily the DCF method. The DCF valuation was based on projected cash flows for the financial years 2026 through 2030 and utilized a WACC of 11.0% as a significant unobservable input, with terminal value determined using a perpetual-growth methodology. The contractual right was initially recognized at a fair value of $1,400,000. As of June 30, 2026, the DCF method indicated a value of $2.06 per underlying share, resulting in a fair value of the derivative asset of $1,442,000. The Company recognized a gain from the change in fair value of $42,000 for the year ended June 30, 2026. The derivative asset was classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.

notes.title: Income Taxes
text: Note 17 – Income taxes
United States of America

The Company was incorporated in the State of Delaware and conducts operations through subsidiaries in multiple jurisdictions, with its principal business operations conducted in Malaysia. Management has determined that the United States represents the Company’s primary tax jurisdiction because the Company is incorporated in the United States and, as a U.S. corporation, is subject to U.S. federal income tax on its worldwide income, including certain income earned through its foreign subsidiaries.

As of June 30, 2026, the operations in the United States of America incurred $25,085,124 of cumulative net operating losses which can be carried forward indefinitely to offset future taxable income and can be used to offset up to 80% of taxable income for losses arising in tax years beginning after June 30, 2023. The deferred tax assets arising from these net operating losses as of June 30, 2026 and 2025 were $5,267,876 and $3,270,173, respectively, for which a full valuation allowance has been provided.

TGL also subject to controlled foreign corporations Subpart F income (“Subpart F”) tax, which is a tax primarily on passive income from controlled foreign corporations with a tax rate of 35%. In addition, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act imposed a global intangible low-taxed income (“GILTI”) tax, which is a tax on certain offshore earnings at an effective rate of 10.5% for tax years (50% deduction of the current enacted tax rate of 21%) with a partial offset for 80% foreign tax credits. If the foreign tax rate is 13.125% or higher, there will be no U.S. corporate tax after the 80% foreign tax credits are applied.
For the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company’s foreign subsidiaries did not generate any income that is subject to Subpart F tax and GILTI tax.
Malaysia

TADAA Technologies, TADAA Capital, Tazte Technology and EVIX Technologies, and TADAA Ventures and Bowlcrafted through their disposal on February 10, 2026, are governed by the income tax laws of Malaysia and the income tax provision in respect of operations in Malaysia is calculated at the applicable tax rates on the taxable income for the periods based on existing legislation, interpretations and practices in respect thereof. Under the Income Tax Act of Malaysia, enterprises that incorporated in Malaysia are usually subject to a unified 24% enterprise income tax rate while preferential tax rates, tax holidays and even tax exemption may be granted on case-by-case basis. As of June 30, 2026, the operations in Malaysia incurred $24,997,967 of cumulative net operating losses which can be carried forward for a maximum period of ten consecutive years to offset future taxable income. The deferred tax assets arising from these net operating losses as of June 30, 2026 and 2025 were $5,999,512 and $5,404,721, respectively, for which a full valuation allowance has been provided.

notes.title: Concentrations of Risks
text: Note 18 – Concentrations of risks

For the year ended June 30, 2026, no customer accounted for 10.0% or more of the Company’s total revenues. For the years ended June 30, 2025, one customer accounted for approximately 63.5% or more of the Company’s total revenues.

As of June 30, 2026, two customers accounted for approximately 86.0% and 13.4% of the total balance of accounts receivable, respectively. As of June 30, 2025, one customer account for approximately 92.3% of the total balance of accounts receivable, respectively

For the years ended June 30, 2026, one vendor accounted for approximately 97.7% of the Company’s total purchases. For the years ended June 30, 2025, two vendors accounted for approximately 52.7% and 41.2% of the Company’s total purchases.

As of June 30, 2026, three vendors accounted for approximately 48.8%, 21.8%, and 15.8% of the total balance of accounts payable. As of June 30, 2025, three vendors accounted for approximately 46.7%, 20.9%, and 15.1% of the total balance of accounts payable.

Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to significant concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash. As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, $1,590,873 and $236,657 were deposited with financial institutions or fund received from customer being held in third party platform’s fund account, $830,937 and $31,115 of these balances are not covered by deposit insurance, respectively. While management believes that these financial institutions are of high credit quality, it also continually monitors their credit worthiness.

Financial instruments that are potentially subject to credit risk consist principally of accounts receivable and other receivables. The Company believes the concentration of credit risk in its accounts receivable and other receivables is substantially mitigated by its ongoing credit evaluation process and relatively short collection terms. The Company does not generally require collateral from customers. The Company evaluates the need for a provision for estimated credit losses based upon factors surrounding the credit risk of specific customers, historical trends and other information.

The Company cannot guarantee that the current exchange rate will remain steady; therefore, there is a possibility that the Company could post the same amount of profit for two comparable periods and because of the fluctuating exchange rate actually post higher or lower profit depending on exchange rate of RM converted to US$ on that date. The exchange rate could fluctuate depending on changes in political and economic environments without notice.

notes.title: Segment Information
text: Note 20 – Segment information

The Company’s operating segments have been identified based on the way management organizes the business by the nature of services provided to customers and how the Chief Operating Decision Maker (“CODM”) manages the business and allocates resources. The CODM for the Company is its Chief Executive Officer . The Company has two reportable segments: (i) payment processing and e-commerce operation on its ZCITY platform, and (ii) customized software development service.

The accounting policies applied to each segment are consistent with those described in the summary of significant accounting policies. The CODM evaluates the performance of reportable segments and allocates resources primarily based on segment profit (loss). Segment profit (loss) represents segment revenue less directly attributable and allocated cost of revenue and operating expenses. Segment profit (loss) is the sole measure used by the CODM and is determined in a manner consistent with the measurement principles used in preparing the consolidated financial statements in accordance with ASC 280-10-50-28A. The CODM does not evaluate the performance of segments using asset information. As such, the Company does not allocate assets to its reportable segments. Intersegment sales and transfers are accounted for as if the transactions were made with third parties, using current market prices.

The Company’s reportable segments represent strategic business units that offer different products and services and are managed separately due to their distinct operational and marketing requirements.

notes.title: Subsequent Events
text: Note 22 – Subsequent Events
The Company evaluated all events and transactions that occurred after June 30, 2026 up through October 13, 2026, the date the Company issued these consolidated financial statements.
Acquisition of Contro Limited

On July 1, 2026, the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, TADAA Limited, completed the acquisition of 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of Contro Limited (“Contro”), a Hong Kong incorporated company, for total cash consideration of $20,000. Contro is a dormant company whose principal asset is a Money Service Business registration with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (“FINTRAC”).
Proposed Acquisition of Cigar Secret Sdn. Bhd.

On July 20, 2026, the Company entered into a Share Sale Agreement to acquire 149,880 ordinary shares of Cigar Secret Sdn. Bhd. (“Cigar Secret”), representing 80% of Cigar Secret’s enlarged share capital, for aggregate consideration of $612,445. Of the total purchase consideration, $551,200 is payable as a deposit upon execution of the agreement and has been settled through the issuance of 149,267 shares of the Company’s common stock at a price of $3.69 per share. The remaining $61,245 is payable in accordance with the terms of the agreement. The completion of the acquisition is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions precedent.
Enter into Software Development Agreement

On August 26, 2026, the Company entered into three separate Software Development Agreements with Mestiz Technology Sdn. Bhd., E Agro Digital Sdn. Bhd. and Add2Cart Commerce Pte. Ltd. for the development of a Lifestyle Membership and Experience Platform. The aggregate contract consideration is $3,000,000, consisting of $1,000,000 under each agreement, payable based on specified milestones in cash, shares of the Company’s common stock, or a combination thereof at the Company’s discretion.

On September 11, 2026, the Company entered into an additional Software Development Agreement with Mestiz Technology Sdn. Bhd. for the development and implementation of a centralized Power BI business intelligence platform for the Company and its subsidiaries. The total contract consideration is $2,000,000, payable based on specified milestones in cash, shares of the Company’s common stock, or a combination thereof at the Company’s discretion.

In connection with these agreements, the Company issued an aggregate of 868,720 shares of common stock, consisting of 233,645 shares to Add2Cart Commerce Pte. Ltd., 233,645 shares to E Agro Digital Sdn. Bhd. and 401,430 shares to Mestiz Technology Sdn. Bhd.
